name: Chufa

facts.how: Raw, roasted, or ground for a nut-milk

caution: Also called yellow nutsedge, a persistent 'weed' whose tubers are the food. Rinse the soil off well; they are safe and sweet. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A grass-like sedge with a triangular stem; the prize is the cluster of pea-sized tubers on the roots, sweet and almond-like.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Eat them raw once washed, roast them, or soak and blend them into horchata-style tiger-nut milk.
